To be honest a lot of people told me that the TMX is better than the G29/G920 (in all ways keep in mind) and there is no going wrong getting the TMX... I can completely vouch that the G29/G920 is much better. I get major FFB cut in the TMX (Within 10 laps) and far far more expensive when equating for the pedals (However to be fair they are better pedals than the G29/G920 but not enough to get it over the G29/G920).

The package you get with the G29/G920 is much better. The pedals are identical (Still the T3PA Pro's are better) and the feel of the wheel... yeah that is very different but not bad.

* Wheel feel = pretty equal when equating for FFB cut you get on the TMX
* Pedals out of the box HUGE difference but TMX upgraded is better
* FFB Fade the TMX gets within 10 laps the G920 I got around 30+ laps and it was fine (Putting a fan for better air flow for the TMX did very little help made it go to 13 laps and not 10 (If I set the FFB to 50-55/60 percent then its much better))
* FFB Sound... Yeah. If you are touchy to this... get the TMX. The G920 is kinda loud
* Wheel feel in terms of quality... not even a competition. The G920 is far superior
* Base quality is pretty equal its just a plastic base... but the TMX clamp is better

Overall the FFB fade on the TMX made me dislike it and the G920 became my new favorite... Well... in terms of lower end wheels.

CSL:E and Clubsport V2 are one of my if not my favorite wheels... Im not rich. cant own a DD wheel... at least... as of now :)

Wheel Suggestions:

&#x200B;

A great wheel for starting out is either the TMX or T150. I also really like the G29 and G920.   


Be warned my TMX only lasted roughly 1 year 7 month's. I had a G27 that last me 6 years then I sold it and it ran another 2 years after that. I would expect the same of the G29 and G920 since they are only a updated version of the G27.

&#x200B;

F1 Game Tips:

&#x200B;

* Find a difficulty that is near the same pace as your teammate (I suggest doing this test on a track you are okay on to help even it out on tracks you are not to good at and tracks you are good at)
* If you use a Wheel (Which is for me the only way to play) then find a comfortable FFB setting (Never run at 100 on a TMX/T150)
* Be patient on the first lap to avoid damage while also trying to atleast maintain position (Unless you Qualied farther back than expected then try to get atleast one or two places)
* Start out (If you do Career) with a mid to back marker team to help with less requirements in terms of race position and quali position (Always try to compete with your teammate though)
*  Experiment With Different Car Set-Ups 
* Manage R&D wisely (Pick the appropriate part for the vehicle you have)
* If a Team is Sportsman sided try to lean that way for better contract negotiations and vice versa
* Pay Attention to your tire status dont overheat them
* Complete most practice sessions and ALWAYS do Quali + Race
* Create Rivalry (That is in fair ground) to maybe be able to replace him (Improve Likability within the team)

For me no I don't get that anymore. When I first started I had it so that in Quali (F1 2017) they would be faster than me and then I would be faster in the Race and in F1 2018 it was equal in Quali and sometimes they would be faster others I am. I have certain tracks I am not to good on though so I believe that may be why that's the case. Generally I at 108 AI difficulty am equal in performance to my teammate either it being Race, Qualy or Practice.

For R&D its kinda simple due to the UI Codemasters gives. They break down your car performance in three areas Aero, Engine and Chassis. If you are lackluster in either generally you want to upgrade that section unless you feel the car needs another upgrade (IE Understeer or Oversteer).

This guide gives a good understanding of it more. https://realsport101.com/news/sports/racing/f1/f1-2018-game-reseach-development-guide/

Now to talk about the Race Cockpit.

[OpenWheeler GEN2](https://www.amazon.com/OpenWheeler-Logitech-Thrustmaster-Controllers-PlayStation-4/dp/B00ORLVWNM/ref=sr_1_9?keywords=racing+cockpit&qid=1555073587&s=gateway&sr=8-9) is a really good one and is supported on almost if not any Race Wheel (Including Fanatec). However if you use a Fanatec dont use a Direct Drive Wheel on this cockpit (I doubt you would get one this early into Sim Racing however for future reference) This one goes for around 300-400 or so USD. Was not able to find a good review on this one. (Its a good cockpit though but is also a little more wobbly than the one below)

[Next Level Racing F1 & GT Style Cockpit](https://www.amazon.com/Next-Level-Racing-F-GT-Simulator-Cockpit/dp/B07FY342LV/ref=sr_1_2_sspa?keywords=racing+cockpit&qid=1555073587&s=gateway&sr=8-2-spons&psc=1) is one I personally use and love. It is the same as the other and supports all wheels (Almost) and is adjustable for roughly 499 USD. (And is F1 & GT style meaning it can switch between the two) [Review](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xwy7I_in2ak)

This is also like the wheel purely based on personal preference due to you being able to go out and make a more sturdy cockpit (That supports Direct Drive Wheels) for roughly 200-400 USD (Including a seat) however you would have to DIY it and not everyone is comfortable doing so.
